claims.answer: Onboarding detects git, gh and installed agents; projects come from a local folder or Git URL and must be git repositories. GitHub is the fully supported host; managed cloud workspaces require Team or Ultra.

first_task_setup.answer: First launch checklist covers gh sign-in, agent detection and adding a project; Cmd+N then starts a workspace with a prompt.

no_git.answer: Projects must be git repositories (FAQ: every project must be a git repository). A folder without git can run as a session workspace instead, which has no project, branch or PR link.

local_git_without_remote.answer: FAQ says remotes other than GitHub work locally; a repo with no remote at all is not addressed.

hosted_git.answer: GitHub is fully supported through gh; other hosts work locally and cross-machine project identity is tied to GitHub; GitLab support is only a tracking issue.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Onboarding uses live detection so the checklist updates as git, gh and agents are installed or signed in.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: Managed cloud needs a Team or Ultra plan, a connected GitHub repository and agent sign-in. Setup uses environments of one to 20 repositories.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Headless install, superset start --daemon and systemd guidance cover a user-provided server without the desktop app.

limitations: Local projects need Git and an installed agent.
Managed cloud requires Team/Ultra, connected GitHub repos and agent sign-in; no onboarding timing test.

claims.answer: Current CLI and OAuth HTTP MCP tools cover tasks, workspaces, agents, terminals, pages, automations and hosts. TypeScript SDK is early alpha, explicitly not for production; no stable REST contract is established.

cli.answer: Installed superset/paradev commands manage tasks, workspaces, terminals, agents, pages, automations and hosts; current CLI docs do not apply a Beta label.

api.answer: HTTP MCP is documented, and the early-alpha SDK exposes configurable API/relay base URLs. A stable independent REST endpoint contract remains unestablished.

sdk.answer: Early-alpha @superset_sh/sdk supports task/workspace/project/host/agent/terminal/automation operations; docs say not production-ready and may be removed.

mcp_server.answer: HTTP MCP at api.superset.sh/mcp exposes the current named task, workspace, agent, terminal, page, automation, host and project tools. No fixed tool count is claimed; v1 returns410.

webhooks.answer: Automations accept inbound POST webhook triggers using a sset_wh_ token, with no filters or de-duplication. The SDK reference does not mention webhooks. Outbound webhook delivery from Paradev is not documented.

operations.answer: MCP/CLI cover task CRUD, workspace create/update/delete, agent launch, terminal read/send, automations and Pages; SDK covers a subset.

authentication.answer: OAuth 2.1 scoped to the active organization for interactive MCP, and sk_live_ API keys (full organization access) for CLI, SDK and CI.

stability.answer: The SDK is explicitly early alpha and not for production. Current CLI docs carry no Beta label; legacy v1 MCP is removed with410, while the documented v2 path remains supported.

limitations: SDK is early alpha and explicitly not meant for production; current CLI docs do not label CLI Beta.
No installed API/CLI or authenticated MCP scenario ran.
The undated roadmap SDK & public API label is not a stable REST contract.

claims.answer: Current Paradev plugins supply MCP tools and skills with agent-specific support and a vendor credential proxy. The chat /mcp command separately lists configured servers; broader MCP manager/community marketplace remain roadmap items.

mcp_client.answer: Built-in chat /mcp lists configured MCP servers from .mastracode/mcp.json, .amp/settings.json or .mcp.json with name, transport and state. Installed plugins add their MCP servers to Claude Code (~/.claude.json) and Codex (~/.codex/config.toml) configs. A general MCP manager is In Progress on the roadmap and not claimed as shipped.

plugins.answer: Install service plugins in the sidebar. Claude/Codex get MCP+skills; Kimi/Vibe/Grok get skills only. User config entries win over managed copies.

custom_tools.answer: Custom plugins can proxy an existing Streamable HTTP MCP server and ship skills/scripts; the tool server itself must be operated separately.

instructions_import.answer: Plugin skills and built-in skills are installed into standard agent discovery paths; user-authored copies are not overwritten.

authentication.answer: Account-requiring plugins connect through Paradev; local configs point at its proxy and do not contain OAuth tokens.

permission_scope.answer: Slack agent plugin tools cannot delete resources, merge pull requests or perform bulk writes.

integration_owner.answer: Paradev manages plugin installation, config entries and credential proxy; the external MCP server owns its tools. Organization repositories are synced by an owner/admin.

limitations: No plugin call or credential boundary test.
MCP manager/community marketplace roadmap scope is broader than the released service-plugin catalog.

local_creation.answer: New task modal and native create operation with title, description, status, priority and assignee.

prompt_intake.answer: The Slack agent and MCP tasks_create can create tasks from natural-language requests; no desktop prompt-to-task flow documented.

external_import.answer: Linear issues are listed beside native tasks (changelog Oct 4: browse and create Linear issues in Tasks with list and board views, import as a Superset task, each member connects their own Linear account); GitHub issues have their own source tab with Add to workspace.

chat_git_triggers.answer: Slack mentions spawn a workspace and agent; a Linear local script can create or reuse a workspace per issue.

authoritative_tracker.answer: An organization owner selects Linear or Superset as the tracker; --tracker can override the selection per CLI command. Full two-way synchronization semantics remain unverified.

stable_ids.answer: Tasks have an org-unique slug (<key>-<number>) and can be fetched by UUID or slug.

sync.answer: The Tasks page describes issues synced from the connected Linear workspace. An organization owner selects Linear or Superset as the tracker, with --tracker overrides per command; full two-way synchronization semantics remain unverified.

supported_edits.answer: With Linear connected, linking an issue or opening its task in a workspace moves the Linear issue to In Progress.

external_roundtrips.answer: The CLI creates, updates and deletes Linear issues through the invoking member's own Linear connection (delete archives them, CLI reference, Tasks). The In Progress write-back and branch-name autolink are documented.

limitations: No authenticated tracker-write or sync-conflict test.
The Linear custom-tool script is separate from native task records and plugin issue tools.

evidence.locator: Hero; FAQ; Supported agents; Download; Source available

evidence.title: Pricing
evidence.locator: Free; Pro; Enterprise; FAQ
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Free: $0, one user, local workspaces, desktop app and CLI, no credit card. Pro: $20 per user per month billed monthly, or $15 per user per month billed yearly ($180 per user billed yearly); billed per active seat; unlimited users, remote access, automations, Linear and Slack integrations, mobile app. Enterprise: custom pricing, annual billing only; SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs, SOC 2 Type II report, uptime SLA with dedicated support. Workspaces and projects unlimited on all plans. Plan changes take effect at the end of the billing period. No free-for-now, trial or deadline wording. Copyright line 2026 only. The "from $15" header noted on Oct 8 was not reproduced.

evidence.title: Superset documentation
evidence.locator: Documentation Sections; Supported Agents
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09 (docs root). Navigation lists Agent Status and Notifications and Pull Requests by title only. No sidebar activity strip, board column or grouping text on this page; linked pages checked separately. No dates.

evidence.title: Tasks
evidence.locator: Sources; Views; Creating and editing; Task to workspace
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. New task modal: title, description, status, priority, assignee. Views: sortable table or kanban board grouped by status. Semantic search ("find tasks by meaning"). Run in workspace: pick a project and agent, one workspace per task, with an Auto-run command toggle. Linear source lists issues from the whole connected workspace ("synced from your connected workspace"; no direction stated); filters for project, status and assignee. GitHub issues source with repository filter and Add to workspace. Task projects not covered. Creating tasks from Slack or MCP not stated on this page.

evidence.title: Remote Access
evidence.locator: Hosts and the relay; Security; Who can access; Ports; Turning access off
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. superset start --daemon registers the machine with the relay. Desktop toggle "Allow remote access to this device via relay"; default state not stated. Only the starting user has access until members are added in Settings, Hosts (Add member); owners can promote or remove members. Terminals, agent runs and the diff viewer are proxied through the relay. iPhone or iPad needs the computer awake, online and running Superset. Turning access off restarts the host service and interrupts in-flight terminals. Port forwarding needs a host on host-service 1.26 or newer; TCP only. Owner-offline behaviour, co-prompting and concurrency not described.

evidence.title: Agent Orchestration
evidence.locator: Roles; Who orchestrates; Live progress; Activation
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. The superset:orchestrate skill lets one agent coordinate workers in separate workspaces through the Superset CLI. The coordinator creates workspaces, launches workers and monitors them with terminals read and send. The coordinator can be Claude Code or Codex; workers can be any mix of agents Superset runs. Workers finish with a structured completion or blocked message that the coordinator verifies. Each worker yields one branch and PR. Model or effort selection not covered. Natural-language invocation wording not reproduced in this read. No dates.

evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09 at pinned commit fc44d32, LICENSE.md: Elastic License 2.0 text (blob unchanged on main).

evidence.title: Superset roadmap
evidence.locator: In Progress; Up Next; Exploring; Recently Shipped
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. In Progress, Up Next and Exploring have no dates; only Recently Shipped (Jul to Aug 2026) is dated. In Progress: In-app PR merge; MCP manager; embedded browser improvements; smoother onboarding. Up Next: next-generation chat; native PR reviews; improved diff viewer; background processes in chat; plugin marketplace. Exploring: project-wide search; work from tickets (Linear); autonomous ticket-to-PR pipeline; automations and event triggers; orchestration chat; agent self-verification; session snapshots and revert; attention queue; cloud sandboxes; SDK and public API; iOS app. The iOS app stays Exploring although the App Store app is documented as shipped. No October 2026 entries.

evidence.title: Install
evidence.locator: Platform and versions; Requirements; First launch; iPhone
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. macOS Apple Silicon and Intel; Linux x64 AppImage experimental; Windows not yet available. Git required; gh CLI optional but needed for PR workflows and offered during onboarding. Onboarding checks prerequisites live: the checklist updates when git, gh or agents are installed or signed in. At least one coding agent needed. iPhone and iPad app: iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later and Superset Pro; enable Remote Access to reach agents on your computer; cloud workspaces in early access. Android not available yet; join the waitlist. No dates.

evidence.title: The Superset Model
evidence.locator: Projects; Workspaces; Terminals; Devices
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. A workspace is an isolated git worktree on its own branch. A workspace lives on the machine that hosts its files, terminals and ports, which need not be the machine you are using. Remote access reaches workspaces hosted on another device. Automations dispatch scheduled agent runs to whichever device you pick. Sessions survive restarts. Cloud workspaces, early access and relay are not described on this page; the "Device filter" wording recorded on Oct 8 was not reproduced here.

evidence.title: Workspaces
evidence.locator: Creation and Branches; Status Indicators; Archiving; Deleting
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Local project workspaces use isolated git worktrees at <worktrees path>/<project>/<branch>. Fresh-branch workspaces start from main; existing branch and review-PR options also exist. A session is a workspace without a project, stored under ~/.superset/sessions, with no branch or PR link. Organization owners and device owners can delete a project. Board columns follow workspace state derived from agent status and PR state: Idle, Working, Needs attention, Needs review, Merged, Deleted; Merged and Deleted are history cards. Cloud workspaces are in early access and not generally available; when available, a new working branch is created from the selected base. Filter menu includes Device.

evidence.title: Diff Viewer
evidence.locator: Diff modes; Staging and committing; Push, pull, and PR creation; Review comments
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Review changes, stage files, commit, push and pull; split and unified layouts; focus mode; open a pull request on GitHub from the viewer. Review tab shows PR review comments, with resolved comments separated from open ones; PR check status appears in the changes sidebar. Selecting lines in a PR Code tab sends feedback to an agent; posting to GitHub is optional. Remote workspace support, image diffs and multiple reviewers are not mentioned on this page.

evidence.title: Pull Requests
evidence.locator: Merging; CI/check status; Review feedback
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Pull Requests view: resizable split view; connect GitHub under project settings to sync PRs. Merge options: Squash and merge, Merge commit, Rebase and merge. Close and reopen are header actions. The Merge action acts on the real PR through the user's GitHub connection, "with the same permissions and effects as merging on github.com." Checks show each CI run with a GitHub link; cancelled checks count as failures. Comment thread with reply composer. PR creation is described in the diff viewer. No dates.

evidence.title: AI Agents
evidence.locator: Supported agents; Launching agents; Custom agents; Permissions
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Lists 22 supported agents: Claude Code, Amp, Codex, Gemini CLI, Mastracode, OpenCode, Pi, Oh My Pi, Copilot, Mistral Vibe, Kimi Code, Grok, Cursor Agent, Droid, Polygraph, Hermes, Muse Code, Devin, fx, Antigravity, Kiro and UFO. Settings, Agents customises built-in agents: command with and without prompt, prompt command suffix, task prompt template, resume args, fork args, model override. Adding entirely new adapters not documented. The page does not claim that any CLI agent works; the homepage says any CLI-based coding agent. Codex picker shows GPT-5.5 under "Retiring 2026-10-14."

evidence.title: Agent Sessions & Forking
evidence.locator: Session persistence; Forking; Cross-agent handoff; Transcripts
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Resume uses an id-based resume command set in Resume Args; failed resumes show "Failed to resume" with Retry. Sessions whose terminal died unexpectedly auto-resume; sessions closed on purpose or agents that exited cleanly stay stopped. Handoff to another agent seeds it with the last 36,000 characters of terminal context as read-only history and warns that output is not redacted. Fork starts a native copy in the same agent with the same conversation; forks copy conversation, not files. Pausing for questions, tool approval or plan review not covered on this page.

evidence.title: Agent Status & Notifications
evidence.locator: Status states; How status is detected; Notifications
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Lifecycle hooks in each agent config report started, finished and waiting for input; hooks exist only for agents launched through Superset (Settings, Agents toggle removes them). Notifications: sounds and a macOS dock badge for workspaces that need attention. Inline prompts: agents can pause to ask questions, request tool approval or ask for plan review in the chat pane, and the workspace is flagged as needing attention. Running and PR state persist across restarts; Clear Status resets a stale running indicator. Each sidebar workspace shows an activity strip. Waiting-for-input signal varies by agent; some agents trigger completion notifications only. No mobile or push notification described.

evidence.title: Automations
evidence.locator: Schedules; Device selection; Retries; Offline machines; Plan requirement
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Schedules stored as RFC 5545 RRules, with Hourly, Daily, Weekdays and Weekly presets and a Custom option; several cadences per automation through Add Trigger. Schedule triggers are the only trigger type described on this page. Run statuses: created (success), creating (handoff in flight), failed (device offline at fire time or handoff broke). Retry all appears when a latest run failed; Run now dispatches immediately. Delivery is at-least-once. A run records only workspace creation, not agent task success. Creating, running or resuming needs Pro or Enterprise. Overlapping-run handling not described.

evidence.title: Usage
evidence.locator: Subscription allowance; Per-agent breakdown; Estimates vs billed; Machine resources
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Add account creates a second login profile for a provider; Make default picks the account new launches use; a running agent keeps its account until relaunched. Quota cards show account email, plan and one meter per window (Session 5h and Weekly for Claude), refreshed every 5 minutes. Token costs are estimates at API list rates; subscription usage shows "Cost to you: $0." Per-model and per-workspace drilldowns; 7, 30 and 90 day ranges; Cost and Tokens toggle; workspace drilldowns list top sessions by cost. Resources view refreshes CPU and memory every 2 seconds and groups processes by project and pane. No spend or token caps described.

evidence.title: Superset MCP Server
evidence.locator: Endpoint and transport; Authentication; Tools (40 total)
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. HTTP endpoint api.superset.sh/mcp with 40 tools across nine groups: tasks 6 (tasks_list, tasks_get, tasks_create, tasks_update, tasks_delete, tasks_statuses_list), workspaces 4, agents 2, terminals 5, pages 9, automations 11 (including automations_logs), projects 1, hosts 1, organization members 1. OAuth 2.1 default, scoped to the active organization; sk_live API keys for headless use grant full organization access. No stability label; versioned URL kept; v1 path returns 410 Gone. No dates. Re-read 2026-10-09 (final review): Chat Integration documents the /mcp slash command in the built-in chat, listing configured MCP servers with names, transport (local or remote) and state (enabled, disabled or invalid), read from .mastracode/mcp.json, .amp/settings.json or .mcp.json.

evidence.title: Superset CLI Reference
evidence.locator: Commands; Auth-related flags; Stability
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. CLI is in Beta; commands and flags still evolving. Top-level groups: scripts, auth, start, stop, status, update, organization, projects, hosts, workspaces (archive is current; delete is an alias), agents, terminals, browser, pages, tasks, automations, settings, completion, schema, config. Cloud workspace archive stops the sandbox within a minute and deletes it after 7 days; sleep stops the sandbox and ends its terminals and agents. hosts list, set-wake and wake. Global --api-key and SUPERSET_API_KEY. agents read returns the saved agent transcript. No platform list and no dates.

evidence.title: Host Server
evidence.locator: Daemon basics; Headless and VPS setup; Systemd; Upgrades
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. superset start --daemon spawns a background daemon, writes a manifest and binds only to loopback; automatic updates off by default. The systemd example runs superset start without --daemon, requires KillMode=process and a CLI newer than 1.30.2. A headless machine uses the standalone installer; the desktop app starts the host itself. The first machine runs projects create and others run projects setup; projects are host-owned. Wake behaviour not described on this page.

evidence.title: TypeScript SDK
evidence.locator: Authentication; Resources; Stability
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. SDK is in early alpha, "not meant for production use and may be removed in the future." Package @superset_sh/sdk for Node, Bun and Deno; browser bundles should not ship API keys. Resource groups: tasks, workspaces, projects, automations, hosts. Options: apiKey, organizationId, timeout (60 seconds default), maxRetries (2 default), logLevel. Client example shows baseURL and relayURL as optional.

evidence.title: Superset SDK Reference
evidence.locator: Resources and methods
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Operations documented: tasks (create, list, retrieve, update, delete, statuses.list); workspaces (list, create, update, delete); projects (list); hosts (list); agents (list, create); terminals (create only); automations (list, retrieve, create, update, delete, run, pause and resume, logs, getPrompt and setPrompt); organization members (list). No REST reference and no webhook mention. Stability: early alpha.

evidence.title: Linear Integration
evidence.locator: Local script handoff; write-back
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. The page describes an existing Linear connection and gives no connection steps or per-member wording. Linking an issue in the New Workspace flow or opening a task in a workspace uses Linear's branch name and moves the issue to In Progress. --skip-branch-prefix keeps Linear's branch format so Linear autolinks the branch. A wrapper script runs superset workspaces create then open; re-running on the same issue reuses the existing workspace. Sync direction and the authoritative tracker not stated. Pro requirement not mentioned.

evidence.title: Slack Integration
evidence.locator: Triggering agents; Permissions and limits; Where agents run
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. The @superset agent can create, update, search and triage tasks; search the web with citations; read thread or channel history; and spin up a cloud workspace to launch a coding agent. Code-change requests default to a workspace and agent. Rich previews unfurl Superset tasks, workspaces and Pages. Limited tool set: plugin tools cannot delete resources, merge pull requests or perform bulk writes. Uses a linked user's connected Linear and GitHub plugins; a Connect button appears when one is missing. Pro requirement not stated on this page. No dates.

evidence.title: Providers
evidence.locator: Supported providers; Credentials; Which agents
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Any CLI agent said to work. Named gateways: Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry; Anthropic-compatible endpoints such as LiteLLM. Variables include ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. No local-model or Ollama mention. The only stated requirement is an Anthropic-compatible API for custom endpoints; the page recommends pinning model versions. No dates.

evidence.title: FAQ
evidence.locator: Data Handling; Platforms; Isolation; Offline Behavior
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. iPhone and iPad app on the App Store, requiring iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later and Superset Pro. Push notifications are coming. Android not available yet. No supported web dashboard. Windows is planned with no date; Linux x64 AppImage experimental and untested; CLI supports Linux x64 and arm64. Local workspace files live on the host; agents send prompts and context to configured providers; remote access via relay is off by default; Superset never proxies model calls. Worktrees are not sandboxes: agents share processes, network and files outside the worktree. Terminals survive restarts through a background daemon. Every project must be a git repository; GitHub is fully supported through gh; repos with other remotes work locally; cross-machine project identity is tied to GitHub. Account deletion is not self-serve; email support. Pro features live in the v2 interface. Telemetry and licence not covered; no pricing or free-tier wording. Change from the Oct 8 record: iPad now described as on the App Store, not coming.

evidence.title: Troubleshooting
evidence.locator: Failure modes; Terminal reconnect and daemon behavior
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Host must be awake, online and connected to the relay; enable the relay under Settings, Remote Access, or run superset start --daemon. Mobile app shows "One step left" for a host that never connected, "Offline" with a last-seen time for an unreachable host, and "Can't check" when status fails to load. A scheduled run on an offline device is recorded as failed; retry from the Automations list. Updater race fixed in recent releases; terminals are held by a background daemon, so quit fully and relaunch. No owner or teammate access statement.

evidence.title: Terminal
evidence.locator: Session persistence; Environment variables
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Sessions survive app restarts: running processes continue, output history and scrollback preserved. If a terminal ends, New shell starts a fresh session in the same pane; recent output stays visible. Agent recovery is covered on a separate page. Host-run terminals, detached-agent behaviour and cloud or remote terminal persistence not described.

evidence.title: Project Lifecycle Scripts
evidence.locator: config.json; Setup and teardown; Secrets
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Setup and teardown commands run automatically when a workspace is created or deleted, sequentially in the workspace directory, for each workspace; teardown also runs when deleting through the CLI, SDK or MCP. Terminal scripts are a separate type. Ports, port allocation, a .env copy step and run scripts are not described on this page.

evidence.title: Port Management
evidence.locator: Detection; Allocation; Forwarding
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. The desktop app forwards detected ports from the selected remote workspace to the local machine. If a local port is busy, choose Use another port, which implies the default keeps the same port number. Relay routing, minimum host-service version and UDP are not stated on this page; it refers readers to remote access for requirements.

evidence.title: Pages
evidence.locator: Publishing; Versions; Comments; Sharing
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Visibility: only you (private draft); anyone in the organization (default); anyone with the link, who can read without signing in and cannot comment or edit. Teammates pin comments to page elements; the agent republishes and replies; automatic comment delivery needs the host and agent session running. Edit permissions for organization members not stated. Public viewers can report a page.

evidence.title: In-App Browser
evidence.locator: Previews; Design Mode; Screenshots and agent control
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Design mode arms an element picker; the agent receives the element DOM, computed styles, React component metadata and a cropped screenshot, plus a note, and can go to an existing terminal or a new session. In-app browser pane for previewing running services, with back, forward, reload, address bar, DevTools pane and detected-port links. Agents can open, read, screenshot and interact with browser panes through superset browser CLI commands. For remote workspaces, detected ports are forwarded while that workspace is selected. No Open Preview button described. No dates.

evidence.title: Skills
evidence.locator: Installation; Bundled skills
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Desktop app provisions skills at launch and keeps them updated. Direct install: npx skills add superset-sh/skills. Claude Code route: /plugin marketplace add superset-sh/superset. Managed copies written to ~/.claude/skills/superset/, ~/.agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/commands/. Listed agents: Claude Code; Codex, Kimi, Vibe and Grok as other agents that read skills; in-app chat, invoked as /superset/feedback. Only the Superset marketplace is named; no community plugins or third-party marketplaces. No dates.

evidence.title: IDE Integration
evidence.locator: Supported editors
evidence.finding: Open-in button opens a workspace in Cursor, VS Code, Zed, Windsurf, Antigravity, Sublime Text, JetBrains IDEs; no editor extensions described.

evidence.title: Your First Parallel Session
evidence.locator: Creating a workspace; Racing agents; Shipping the winner
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Cmd+N creates an isolated git worktree on its own branch. Prompt-first flow: describe the task, pick an agent and create; the agent starts immediately. A project can be added from a local folder or a cloned remote. No dates or versions.

evidence.title: Clear PR Feedback in the Background
evidence.locator: Review feedback workflow; CI failures
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Steps: Cmd+N, choose Pull request, search or paste the PR URL; prompt an agent to address each comment; check the Changes tab; push from the diff viewer if the agent did not; re-request review on GitHub; delete the workspace once the PR merges. The page does not say whether feedback sent from the Code tab or diff posts replies to GitHub. No dates.

Sep 28: Superset Mobile live on the App Store; Google Calendar triggers removed; Slack page links unfurl. Sep 6: PR creation and inline review replies; image diffs; per-launch model choice from CLI, SDK and MCP. Aug 30: organization menu, command palette and dock or launcher reachable on Linux and Windows. Aug 27: "Superset has completed its SOC 2 Type II audit"; report available through the trust center. Aug 23: PR merge, close and reopen from the detail header; experimental event triggers (see changelog-events). Entries older than the Aug 2 truncation marker were not read.

evidence.title: Superset for iPhone
evidence.locator: Starting agents; Reviewing diffs; Requirements
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Requires iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later, and Superset Pro. iPhone: available now through the App Store. iPad: available now; runs natively in portrait and landscape. Android: not yet released; waitlist ("Be first to know when it ships"). Features: start agents, follow them live, review the diff from iPhone or iPad. Reply to a waiting agent appears in a testimonial only; notifications not mentioned; "Your code stays on your machines." No launch date. Change from the Oct 8 record: the page now states iPad availability.

evidence.title: Privacy Policy
evidence.locator: Data collected; Code and prompt handling; Deletion; Analytics
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Policy last updated 2026-09-29. Analytics providers such as PostHog process usage data linked to the account identifier; device identifiers and OS version collected; diagnostics shared only when the user chooses. Cookies used for tracking. Messages sent to AI agents "are transmitted to and stored by our services so they can be delivered to your workspaces." Accounts permanently deleted after a 30-day recovery period. Data retained as long as necessary. Google user data not used to train generalized AI models; AI providers do not train on it. Names PostHog and Apple (speech recognition for dictation); refers to a Subprocessors page not read. No statement about Pages uploads. Desktop app described as running locally; no statement about where cloud workspaces run.

evidence.title: Superset releases
evidence.locator: desktop-v1.37.0; desktop-v1.36.0; cli-v1.37.0
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09 (releases page). desktop-canary published 2026-10-09, prerelease, internal build from main. desktop-v1.37.0 published 2026-10-08 05:21 UTC, marked Latest and not a prerelease; notes include mobile voice mode over OpenAI Realtime, CLI rename of workspaces delete to archive, PR-closed automation trigger. cli-v1.37.0 and cli-latest published 2026-10-08, prerelease. desktop-v1.36.0 published 2026-10-06: native iPad fixes for iOS 27, Linux clipboard fix, cloud workspace sleep command. desktop-v1.35.0 and v1.34.0 published 2026-10-02: archive cloud workspaces; run natively on iPad; Windows and Linux app-menu and window-control changes. Release notes describe Windows-specific UI work but do not state Windows availability.

evidence.title: Superset issues
evidence.locator: Open issues listing 2026-10-08
evidence.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09. Header shows 435 open issues; the Oct 8 record counted about 908. evidence.locator: Open a Chat; Supported Agents
evidence.finding: Chat runs the installed CLI through Agent Client Protocol with the same login, settings and MCP servers. CLI/Chat switching resumes the same session. Chat is documented for Claude Code >=2.1.226, Codex >=0.160.0, OpenCode >=1.15.5 and Pi; other agents use terminals.

evidence.title: Paradev Agent Sessions & Forking
evidence.locator: Resume Interrupted Sessions; Fork; Continue with another agent; Read an Agent transcript
evidence.finding: Resume uses native session IDs and configured resume args after unexpected terminal death. Fork copies the conversation, not files, within the same workspace. Cross-agent handoff seeds a fresh session with up to 36,000 context characters; Claude/Codex saved conversations are preferred, otherwise terminal output. Output is not redacted. agents read retrieves Claude/Codex saved transcripts only.

evidence.title: Paradev Agent Status & Notifications
evidence.locator: The Activity Strip; How Status Is Detected; Notifications
evidence.finding: Sidebar activity strips show running agents and ports; running/PR state persists across restarts. Hooks and command wrappers report started, finished and waiting states only for agents launched through Paradev. Waiting-state support varies; inline prompts mark workspaces needing attention.

evidence.title: Paradev Workspaces
evidence.locator: Core Concept; Create Workspaces; Import Worktrees; List and Board Views; PR Status; Restore a Workspace
evidence.finding: Local project tasks use separate Git worktrees and branches; cloud workspaces use separate clones and scratch sessions use managed folders. Board docs name Idle, Working, Needs attention, Needs review, Merged and Deleted. Workspace PR badges link pull requests and deployment previews; archived cards can restore committed work if the branch still exists. Existing worktrees can be imported without moving their paths.

evidence.title: Paradev Agent Orchestration
evidence.locator: Install; What to Ask For; How It Works
evidence.finding: The bundled superset:orchestrate skill makes Claude Code or Codex coordinate mixed-agent workers. The coordinator creates one branch/workspace per worker, launches bounded prompts, reads/sends terminal messages and verifies structured done/blocked reports before integration. Each worker produces a branch and PR. Natural-language examples are documentation, not observed runs.

evidence.title: Paradev Skills
evidence.locator: Installation; What You Get; Using Skills; How They Are Delivered
evidence.finding: Desktop provisions and updates skills at launch; standalone installation uses paradevai/skills or paradevai/paradev marketplace. superset:orchestrate is an installed orchestration skill, selected from context or invoked explicitly. Managed locations include ~/.claude/skills/superset/, ~/.agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/commands/.

evidence.title: Paradev CLI reference
evidence.locator: auth login; workspaces create; agents create; terminals read/send
evidence.finding: CLI authenticates with browser OAuth or an API key and active organization. Workspace and agent creation accept --agent, --model and --effort overrides, subject to harness support. --from-terminal can seed a cross-agent session; terminal read/send monitor and communicate with workers.

evidence.title: Paradev In-App Browser
evidence.locator: Design Mode; Ports Integration; Drive it from the CLI and agents
evidence.finding: Detected ports open in browser panes; remote workspace ports forward while selected. CLI browser screenshot writes a PNG. Design Mode sends an element DOM, computed styles, React metadata and cropped screenshot to an agent. This documents capture and preview, not retained recording or a general evidence gallery.

evidence.title: Paradev Diff Viewer
evidence.locator: Diff Layouts; Review Tab; Send PR Feedback to an Agent
evidence.finding: Split/unified diffs, staging, commit/push/PR actions and GitHub-synced review comments are documented. Selected PR lines can be sent to an agent with file, line range and diff side. A PR without a linked workspace gets a checkout workspace.

evidence.title: Paradev Pages
evidence.locator: Find Workspace Pages; Share a Page; Keep Iterating on the Same Page
evidence.finding: Pages publish an HTML file or directory and link back to the workspace. The workspace menu lists its pages, pinned pages and All pages. Republishing the same source/workspace preserves a URL and earlier versions; versions can be listed and pulled. Public readers access only the shared version. Agent comment delivery requires a running host/session.

evidence.title: Paradev FAQ
evidence.locator: Accounts and Billing; Workspaces and Git; Remote and Automations
evidence.finding: Local CLI works regardless of relay connectivity; remote access is opt-in. Git worktrees are not security sandboxes. Settings > Billing supports cancellation; account deletion, email changes and moving projects between organizations require support.

evidence.title: Paradev Remote Access
evidence.locator: Overview; Option 2 CLI; Headless; Grant teammates access
evidence.finding: Remote hosts authenticate and register with Paradev relay; headless API keys are documented. Organization members need explicit host grants. Relay proxies remote terminals/agents/diffs. Mobile access to a user host requires that host awake and online; managed cloud is separate.

evidence.title: Paradev Pricing
evidence.locator: Compare plans > Usage; FAQ > plan changes
evidence.finding: The comparison table labels Workspaces and Projects unlimited. This is a plan allowance, not observed simultaneous-agent throughput. Free lists one user; paid tiers differ. Upgrades apply immediately; downgrades and cancellation apply at the current billing period end.

evidence.title: Paradev Changelog
evidence.locator: November 1, 2026 > A New Workspaces List; Experimental chat; September 6 > Image, Video, and PDF Diffs
evidence.finding: November 1 describes saved workspace views, status/host/project filters and list/board grouping. It still labels chat experimental under Settings > Experimental > Chat. September 6 documents image before/after diffs and video/PDF previews behind a Preview button. Read through the current November 1 entry; older dated entries are historical.

evidence.title: Paradev MIT licence at desktop-v2.0.5
evidence.locator: LICENSE.md:1-21
evidence.finding: The current stable root licence is MIT, copyright 2025-2026 Superset Inc. It permits use, modification and redistribution subject to its notice requirement. Historical ELv2 text at fc44d32 does not describe this release.

evidence.locator: License & what is free forever
evidence.finding: README says the app is in the repository under MIT and can be forked, modified, self-hosted and redistributed; local parallel agents remain free and paid features are optional services. This is vendor documentation, not an observed self-host deployment.

evidence.finding: Pinned schema retains task branch and prUrl fields. Current Tasks docs expose Run in workspace and GitHub issue Add to workspace. Schema fields alone do not establish a task-linked artifact gallery or exact-revision binding.

evidence.finding: Latest stable resolves to desktop-v2.0.5, November 5, 2026, at 624219c3c6a5428aec38b5f13f040cc0fc087010. Changes include MIT relicensing and importing worktrees from other tools. Live docs can change independently of this release.

evidence.title: Paradev: mcp-server
evidence.locator: Setup; Available tools; OAuth
evidence.finding: Current HTTP MCP server documents tasks/workspaces/agents/terminals/pages/automations/hosts/projects tools and OAuth. Avoiding an exact tool count prevents a stale inventory from being treated as a contract. Legacy v1 returns410.

evidence.title: Paradev: sdk/reference
evidence.locator: Client; Telemetry; tasks CRUD and filters
evidence.finding: Early-alpha SDK has apiKey,organizationId, baseURL api.superset.sh,relayURL,timeout/maxRetries. tasks create/update/list/retrieve/soft-delete expose task status,priority,estimate,dueDate,assignee and labels. SUPERSET_TELEMETRY=0 disables SDK method-call telemetry only.

evidence.title: Paradev: cli/cli-reference

evidence.finding: Current CLI reference does not label CLI Beta. Uses same backend as desktop, OAuth or API key; task tracker can be native or Linear. Commands target local/remote/cloud; tasks support create/update/assignee,status,JSON and tracker override.

evidence.title: Paradev: plugins/build-a-plugin
evidence.locator: Manifest; MCP server; skill scripts
evidence.finding: Users create plugin manifests pointing to existing Streamable HTTP MCP servers, with optional skills/scripts and connector binding. Paradev proxies credentials, no OAuth settings in manifest; it does not bundle the tool server.

evidence.title: Paradev: plugins/organization-plugins
evidence.locator: Roles; synchronization; credentials
evidence.finding: Owners/admins add GitHub plugin repositories. Owner/admin/member plugin access states unavailable/available/installed; unavailable immediately blocks tool use and removes installations on next sync. evidence.title: Paradev: skills

evidence.title: Paradev: editor

evidence.finding: File search and a search bar across open workspaces are documented; editor detects concurrent disk edits and offers compare/reload/overwrite while retaining buffer. No automatic merge. Exact semantic code indexing remains unestablished.

evidence.title: Paradev: tasks
evidence.locator: Create tasks; task detail; Run in workspace
evidence.finding: Native task has editable title/description,status,priority,assignee and labels, alongside connected Linear issues. Run in workspace separately selects a project/agent and one workspace per task, with optional staged auto-run.

evidence.title: Paradev: bring-your-own-cloud
evidence.locator: Overview; Requirements; host start; Security
evidence.finding: Paid Remote Access runs Linux x64/arm64 hosts in user cloud with git/gh and native agent logins. Repos/signins remain on server; relay carries device traffic. Host bindsloopback/outbound relay, systemd enables reboot persistence; access grants expose host authority.

evidence.title: Paradev: cloud-workspaces
evidence.locator: Environments; snapshot; machine sizes; limits; lifecycle; credentials
evidence.finding: Team/Ultra cloud environments clone1-20repos, choose region,variables and machine size2/4,4/8,8/16CPU/GB with64GBdisk. Saved environments snapshot ready files. Idle stop after~hour retains30days; archived disk restorable7days. GB-hour limit stops running workspace~10min later. Credentials are outgoing-proxy placeholders.

evidence.title: Paradev: agent-sessions
evidence.locator: Resume; Fork; Continue with another agent
evidence.finding: Unexpected terminal death relaunches native resume command; failure offers Retry. Native fork retains conversation but shares workspace files. Cross-agent continuation sends last36000chars read-only context, no redaction, checks actual files; saved transcript reading only Claude/Codex.

evidence.title: Paradev: setup-teardown-scripts
evidence.locator: Run Script; Setup ordering
evidence.finding: Setup/teardown run sequentially; Run starts restartable dedicated service terminals. Agents start parallel to setup by default; experimental wait-for-setup starts them only on success. No automatic dependency repair implied.

evidence.title: Paradev: ports
evidence.locator: Overview; deterministic ranges; Remote Access
evidence.finding: Paradev discovers listening workspace processes rather than assigning port ranges; user scripts may reserve/release them. Remote forwarding offers Use another port if local binding is busy.

evidence.title: Paradev: pages
evidence.locator: Design Loop; Share; Comments; Versions; Tool consent
evidence.finding: Pages retain versions under one link, support pinned comment threads routed to listening agents and explicit shared versions. Publicreaders cannot edit/comment/history. Tool consent is perpage/plugin includingfutureversions/writes; UI revocation unavailable.

evidence.title: Paradev: pull-requests
evidence.locator: List filters; Summary; Code; Comment straight to an agent
evidence.finding: PR list filters state/repository/author/review status and shows CI and diffsize. Summary contains checks/runlinks,reviews,comments/threads/commits and up to3 workspacePages. Line comments can send precise context to existing/new agent; narrowpanes stack; mergeusesGitHubpermissions.

evidence.finding: The body explicitly gives October 26, 2026 as the effective date when Superset became Paradev. evidence.title: Paradev Tasks

evidence.finding: Tasks view offers list and status-grouped board views, filters for project, task state, assignee and label that persist, a label hierarchy from path-style names, semantic search and multi-select.

evidence.finding: Home page says code and agent sessions in local workspaces stay on the user's machine, cloud workspaces run in a sandbox, model calls go straight to the user's provider and Paradev does not proxy API calls; it no longer states metadata-only cloud sync.

evidence.finding: Paradev says it completed its SOC 2 Type II audit with an independent auditor and that the report can be requested via trust.paradev.com; scope and period are not given.

evidence.title: Paradev built-in Antigravity agent
evidence.locator: builtin-terminal-agents.ts Antigravity entry; packages/agent-setup/src/agent-wrappers-agy.ts; official agent-integration Supported Agents
evidence.finding: The shipped built-in agent registry explicitly names Antigravity and launches its agy CLI. Its setup package installs corresponding lifecycle hooks. Other unlisted agents can be configured through the generic custom-agent facility.

evidence.title: Paradev shipped account-free local core
evidence.locator: Recently Shipped: Offline / local-first mode, Aug 2026
evidence.finding: The shipped roadmap explicitly says the complete core loop of importing a repository, running an agent and reviewing its diff works signed out and offline. This is usable local core functionality on the user machine, beyond MIT permission alone. Relay, Pages and managed Cloud remain separate vendor services.

evidence.title: Paradev shared host terminal instructions
evidence.locator: terminal.ts writeInput protectedProcedure; official remote-access Grant teammates access and continue workspace sections
evidence.finding: Host members granted access can open the same remote workspaces and terminal sessions. The authenticated writeInput operation accepts workspace/terminal IDs and writes into that session without a creator-only check. Multiple granted humans can therefore send instructions to the same running agent terminal. The host must remain awake and online.

evidence.title: Paradev desktop telemetry controls are no-ops
evidence.locator: settings router lines 1328-1340; main/lib/analytics/index.ts isTelemetryEnabled and track; shared/constants.ts DEFAULT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED
evidence.finding: getTelemetryEnabled always returns true and setTelemetryEnabled returns success without changing state. Main-process analytics checks the compile-time true default, not an end-user setting. The SDK SUPERSET_TELEMETRY=0 control affects SDK method events only, not desktop analytics.

evidence.title: Paradev managed-cloud VM architecture

evidence.finding: The application's cloud engineering guide explicitly describes the sandbox VM, memory limits and swap configuration. The shipped backend provisions and resumes those environments through @vercel/sandbox. This concerns managed Cloud workspaces, not local worktree security.

superset:PLAN-01.answer: Native tasks sit alongside live Linear issues (browse and create in Tasks, per-member Linear connection, changelog Oct 4) and GitHub issues; Slack and MCP can create tasks. A Linear local script can start or reuse a workspace per issue, and the native Linear integration moves the issue to In Progress. The Tasks page says Linear issues are synced from the connected workspace, but sync direction and the authoritative tracker are not documented.
limitations: Which tracker is authoritative, sync direction and external roundtrips are undocumented; the Tasks page's 'synced from your connected workspace' gives no direction.
Task IDs inferred from schema and MCP docs, not tested.

Roadmap lists "Work from tickets" (start a workspace from a Linear ticket; agent reports back with a PR) and "Autonomous ticket-to-PR pipeline" under Exploring. Answer is scoped to what ships: manual or script-initiated workspace start from an issue and the In Progress write-back; automatic report-back with a PR is not claimed.
superset:PLAN-01.external_roundtrips: Only the In Progress write-back and branch-name autolink are documented.

superset:PLAN-07.answer: Agents can list, read, create, update and soft-delete tasks over MCP, CLI and SDK; claiming, dependencies and child tasks were not found.

superset:PLAN-03.answer: Task projects group tasks with state, lead and dates; parent/child and dependency features were not found.
superset:PLAN-03.epics: Task projects (planned state, lead, start/target dates) group tasks and appear as a filter; not labelled epics.

superset:PLAN-06.answer: Native tasks support create, edit, priority, assignee, semantic search, project, status and assignee filters, list and board views, and explicit dispatch to a workspace. Comments and labels are evidenced only by the pinned desktop source (fc44d32), not by docs.
superset:PLAN-06.project_epic_views: List and kanban board by status; task projects exist; epics unverified.

superset:ACC-06.answer: The built-in chat /mcp command lists the workspace's configured MCP servers (names, transport, and enabled, disabled or invalid state). Superset ships skills as a Claude Code plugin and connects Slack-side Linear/GitHub plugins with restricted tools. MCP manager and plugin marketplace are roadmap items.

superset:RUN-03.answer: Terminals run in a background daemon that survives app restarts and updates; unexpected agent-terminal deaths auto-resume for agents with a resume command.

superset:RUN-04.answer: Setup and teardown commands run per workspace on create and delete (install dependencies there). Run scripts run on demand from the Run button in a dedicated pane, not on workspace creation. Detected ports are forwarded to the same local port unless busy. Superset does not assign per-workspace port ranges. The overview example config copies the root .env file in setup, which is user-written script content. Duplicate-install warnings were not reproduced in the Oct 9 read.

superset:RUN-06.answer: Usage shows local Claude Code and Codex token cost, quotas and per-model/workspace breakdowns; automation run history shows failures; logs and traces beyond that were not found.

superset:COORD-05.answer: Agents can pause for questions, tool approval and plan review; workspaces needing input are flagged and notified; unexpected terminal deaths auto-resume. Pause/stop controls were not found.

superset:COORD-07.answer: A quick task takes a prompt and an agent in one step; agents are configurable and skills are discoverable. Growing-epic and live-role views were not found.

superset:ACC-02.answer: Paradev documents 22 built-in terminal agents, custom CLI agents and mixed-harness orchestration. Status and session integration vary by agent; the newer chat interface supports four harnesses and is still labelled experimental in the November 1 changelog.

harnesses.answer: The current AI Agents page lists 22 built-ins, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI; custom CLI agents can be added.

model_providers.answer: Provider gateway instructions cover Claude Code with OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Anthropic-compatible APIs. Other harnesses use their own provider settings; chat has its own Anthropic key flow. No universal provider matrix was verified.

custom_adapters.answer: Settings > Agents > Add agent > Custom agent adds a command with prompt transport and resume/fork args. Custom agents receive a workspace, worktree and terminal; built-in integrations are not implied.

session_integration.answer: Status hooks, resume/fork and handoff are harness-specific. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi can use ACP chat with minimum CLI versions. November 1 changelog labels chat experimental; no chat scenario was run.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Documentation permits Claude Code or Codex coordinators with mixed-agent workers and cross-agent handoff. This is documented, not observed mixed-harness execution.

limitations: Integration depth varies by harness; custom commands do not gain all built-in integrations.
Chat is experimental in the November 1 changelog and requires supported CLI versions.
No installed-client or mixed-harness test was performed.

superset:COORD-01.answer: Paradev documents parallel agents in separate local worktrees, with sidebar activity and workspace list/board views. Pricing lists unlimited workspaces; simultaneous-agent throughput was not measured.

concurrent_sessions.answer: AI Agents explicitly describes agents running in parallel in multiple workspaces. No observed concurrency count is claimed.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Separate local project tasks use their own Git worktree, branch and terminals. Cloud workspaces use clones and scratch sessions are distinct.

quotas.answer: Pricing lists unlimited workspaces and projects. That does not establish a maximum simultaneous-agent count; provider limits and host capacity were not measured.

observed_concurrency.answer: Observed concurrency: Not established in the November 7 pass over current Paradev documentation, pricing, roadmap, changelog, public issues and stable-release source. No installed-client scenario was run.

status_visibility.answer: Sidebar activity shows agents and ports; hooks report running/finished/waiting with harness-specific coverage. November 1 changelog describes saved workspace views and status filters; workspace docs also describe list/board state columns.

limitations: Unlimited workspaces is a vendor plan allowance, not a measured concurrency limit.
Status depends on harness hooks; local worktrees do not prevent merge conflicts.
No installed-client concurrency test.

scope.plan: Remote relay access requires Pro or a higher plan

roles.answer: A skill-driven coordinator directs workers in separate workspaces. Provider-native Claude/Codex subagents are a separate integration.

model_harness_effort.answer: CLI and MCP launches accept agent, model and reasoning-effort overrides subject to harness support. Orchestration docs do not establish an automatic model-selection policy.

messages.answer: The coordinator reads worker terminals and sends prompts or dependency results through CLI terminals read/send.

results_return.answer: Workers report structured completion or blocked messages for coordinator verification before integration.

cross_harness.answer: Claude Code or Codex can coordinate any mix of supported worker agents.

orchestration_owner.answer: An agent using the bundled superset:orchestrate skill drives the CLI; this is skill-based orchestration.

activation.answer: Desktop provisions skills at launch; standalone agents install paradevai/skills or the Paradev Claude marketplace. Natural-language skill selection is documented.

authentication.answer: CLI documents browser OAuth or API-key authentication and active-organization selection. Remote hosts register through authenticated relay access and explicit host grants. No end-to-end delegated auth fixture was run.

live_progress.answer: Coordinator monitoring uses terminals read/send. Claude/Codex provider-native subagents appear under the parent; November 1 adds their activity panel. A retained cross-worker relationship view was not verified.

retained_results.answer: Docs describe a branch and PR per worker. Saved transcripts can be retrieved for Claude/Codex, but complete post-session child findings and their retention period were not tested.

followup.answer: Coordinator sends follow-ups through terminals send. Reopening a completed child and following up after completion was not tested.

invocation.answer: Docs show natural-language fan-out examples and skills selected from context, including running three refactors in parallel. Neither documented invocation nor the shared natural-language fixture was executed.

limitations: Installed orchestration skill, distinct from provider-native subagents and future orchestration-chat UI.
No delegated run, child identity check, completed-child reopening or result-retention fixture.
Model/effort overrides are documented; orchestration selection policy is not.

cli.answer: Installed superset/paradev commands manage tasks, workspaces, terminals, agents, pages, automations and hosts; current CLI docs do not apply a Beta label.

api.answer: HTTP MCP is documented, and the early-alpha SDK exposes configurable API/relay base URLs. A stable independent REST endpoint contract remains unestablished.

sdk.answer: Early-alpha @superset_sh/sdk supports task/workspace/project/host/agent/terminal/automation operations; docs say not production-ready and may be removed.

mcp_server.answer: HTTP MCP at api.superset.sh/mcp exposes the current named task, workspace, agent, terminal, page, automation, host and project tools. No fixed tool count is claimed; v1 returns410.

stability.answer: The SDK is explicitly early alpha and not for production. Current CLI docs carry no Beta label; legacy v1 MCP is removed with410, while the documented v2 path remains supported.

custom_tools.answer: Custom plugins can proxy an existing Streamable HTTP MCP server and ship skills/scripts; the tool server itself must be operated separately.

instructions_import.answer: Plugin skills and built-in skills are installed into standard agent discovery paths; user-authored copies are not overwritten.

integration_owner.answer: Paradev manages plugin installation, config entries and credential proxy; the external MCP server owns its tools. Organization repositories are synced by an owner/admin.

instructions.answer: Paradev-managed skills teach agents to use orchestration, setup, pages and feedback. This does not establish project-wide maintained memory.

scope.answer: Skills are provisioned per machine into the agent discovery directories; organization plugins are visible only within their organization and role settings.

provenance.answer: Organization plugin sources show the GitHub admin used for sync and recorded plugin versions; this is plugin provenance, not a verified knowledge-memory citation system.

freshness.answer: Built-in managed skills refresh every launch; organization repositories sync only on admin action and preserve the last good version on failure. Per-repo learned agent memory remains roadmap work.

code_search.answer: File search and cross-open-workspace search are documented; no code-symbol/architecture retrieval guarantee or indexing method is stated.

conflict_detection.answer: If an agent changes an open file with unsaved edits, the editor shows an external-change banner and compare/reload/overwrite choices. It does not merge edits automatically.

idea_parking.answer: Tasks can be created and edited independently of Run in workspace; their initial status may be backlog. No separate idea inbox is documented.

task_session_separation.answer: Task records exist before a separately invoked Run in workspace creates an agent workspace. Workspaces can link a taskId; a task is not the terminal conversation.

metadata.answer: Task fields include title,description,status,priority,assignee,estimate,due date and labels.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: Paradev-native tasks can be created directly; Linear is an alternative tracker selected or overridden through the CLI, not a requirement.

assign.answer: Tasks create/update accept assigneeId through the SDK shared backend; CLI tasks similarly update assignment.

human_visibility.answer: The desktop Tasks detail exposes editable task fields/activity alongside the same native tasks addressed by CLI/SDK.

attribution.answer: SDK task list returns creator and assignee names/images; action-by-action concurrent agent attribution is not established.

self_hosted.answer: A paid Remote Access host can run on Linux in the user own cloud account; data/credentials remain there but discovery and device traffic still depend on Paradev relay/API.

hybrid.answer: The desktop/mobile clients open either own-host workspaces or vendor cloud workspaces; those have separate provisioning and billing.

provisioning.answer: Create cloud environment with repositories, region and variables, then choose project, branch, environment and size for each cloud workspace. Own servers are installed/configured separately.

region.answer: Cloud environment chooses a region at creation, default nearest; saved snapshot environments keep their region fixed. The guide does not enumerate all locations.

other_device_continuation.answer: Cloud workspaces remain running with the laptop closed and can be opened from desktop,iPhone or iPad; own cloud hosts appear in those clients too.

secrets.answer: Cloud sandboxes see placeholder agent/GitHub credentials and Paradev adds real credentials to outgoing requests; environment variables/secrets are copied into workspaces, with named provider-token overrides ignored.

expiry.answer: Cloud idle stop retains files30days; archive can restore disk within7days before deletion. This does not guarantee multi-day task outcome continuity.

context_loss.answer: Cross-agent continuation includes at most36000characters of recent context and no credential redaction, while native fork retains conversation. Runtime/process restoration after crash depends on native resume support.

duplicate_actions.answer: Automation documentation explicitly says at-least-once delivery may dispatch a run more than once and prompts should be safe to rerun; exactly-once actions are not promised.

snapshots.answer: Save as environment snapshots a fully started cloud workspace so later workspaces avoid fresh setup. Repositories/region are fixed in the saved environment.

services.answer: Run commands start dev servers or long-running services on demand in a dedicated pane and can stop/restart without recreating the workspace.

duplicate_installs.answer: Fresh cloud environments start clean and rerun setup; a saved ready-workspace snapshot can avoid that repeated setup. No general shared package-cache contract is stated.

collisions.answer: Local workspace ports are discovered, not allocated. Setup scripts can reserve ranges; remote forward conflicts offer another free local port. Concurrent service isolation was not tested.

retries.answer: Automation Run now/Retry all manually redispatch failed runs; missed offline runs are not retried automatically and schedule advances. Unexpected agent terminal death has native resume plus Retry on failure.

provider_failures.answer: A failed native agent resume shows Failed to resume and a Retry action; exact provider error/backoff handling is not established.

unauthorized_access.answer: Only owners/admins add organization plugin repositories; setting a role Unavailable immediately blocks plugin tools. This is plugin access control, not a tested complete project-RBAC boundary.

delivery.answer: Chat delivers approvals inline; Pages tool consent is a dialog for the viewing user before a page/plugin tool call.

approver_identity.answer: Page plugin calls run as the signed-in viewer through their own connected account; this does not establish attributed command-approval logs.

lifetime.answer: Page/plugin consent persists for every tool of that plugin, including writes and future versions of the page; no per-command expiry is specified.

revoke.answer: The Pages guide explicitly says removing a page tool access from the app is unavailable. Organization plugin Unavailable immediately stops tools for that role.

tunnels.answer: Remote workspace traffic and forwarded TCP ports traverse Paradev relay; turning access off restarts/stops host service and interrupts host-backed work.

defaults.answer: Remote relay access is off by default; a new organization plugin is available only to owners/admins. These are access defaults, not universal harness command policy.

edits.answer: Republishing a Page creates a version; earlier versions remain readable to authorized users. This is document history, not a full workspace activity audit.

discussion.answer: Pinned Page comment threads include agent replies and resolved/open state, with context sent to listening agents.

cross_user_persistence.answer: Organization members share the same Page link/version history and comment threads; public anonymous readers receive only the selected shared version.

export.answer: pages pull can retrieve a chosen published version; no bulk audit/activity export is established.

mutability.answer: A Page source path republishes into the same page with new version history, while shared links can follow latest or stay pinned. This is not tamper-evident audit retention.

request_changes.answer: Select diff lines and send feedback to a running/new agent, optionally posting on GitHub; the agent receives file, range and side. A complete review-decision fixture was not run.

shipping_guidance.answer: PR header offers Start Workspace and Merge; Changes menu offers applicable commit/push/createPR actions. No exact-revision acceptance gate is documented.

build_links.answer: PR Summary lists CI check states with links to their GitHub runs; this does not establish links to deployed production builds.

commit_links.answer: PR activity includes commits together with review/comment threads. An immutable task-to-delivery receipt is not established.

summaries.answer: PR Summary shows authored description,checks and reviews; no automatic batch change summary test was run.

risk_size_filters.answer: PR list shows added/deleted line counts and filters review status/repository/author; a dedicated risk/size filtering control is not established.

artifacts.answer: PR pane displays up to three workspace Pages and links to all. This does not establish all reviewer outputs as structured artifacts.

request_changes.answer: Per-line feedback can be routed to an agent in the linked/new PR workspace. Multi-task batching and exact-revision approval were not tested.

next_actions.answer: Start Workspace, Merge and close/reopen PR actions are shown in PR detail; review filters retain their state between visits.

export.answer: Published Page versions can be retrieved with pages pull, and local code remains ordinary git files. A full task/session-history export/import contract is not established.

credentials.answer: Plugin credentials remain on Paradev servers behind a proxy. Local agents retain per-account native credentials; cloud sandboxes receive placeholders and outgoing requests carry the real credentials.

residency.answer: Cloud environment region is chosen at creation and fixed for saved snapshots; BYOC repo and sign-in state live in the user server. This does not establish all metadata/subprocessor residency.

telemetry_controls.answer: SUPERSET_TELEMETRY=0 disables SDK method-call telemetry. This does not establish a disable control for desktop analytics.
